title: Verify, protect and approve AI output
nav: 5. Verify, protect and approve AI output
objective: Find three reasons to reject a polished generated executive deck.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: People remain accountable for anything that goes to a customer, and for every decision. Review AI output systematically before you use it.

items: **Factual support:** does the cited passage actually support the claim?
**Permissions:** may this content be shared with this audience?
**Confidentiality:** does it contain customer or internal information that must not be shared?
**Technical feasibility:** has the SE verified each capability?
**Arithmetic and units:** are the calculations correct?
**Bias and framing:** are downside results kept?
**Claims and clearance:** are external claims approved?

blocks.x: A draft can pass citation review and still fail, for example because it includes internal pilot thresholds or restricted customer details. Classify each section as learner-safe, author-only, or pending clearance.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Never give AI authority to submit pilot approvals, send customer messages, change systems, or produce an SME sign-off. Consequential actions go through authorized human processes.
Polish isn't proof. Run every AI-assisted output through the same checks before anyone outside the team sees it.

blocks.title: Review checks for AI output
blocks.alt: Eight cards listing review checks for AI-assisted output: factual support, freshness, permissions, confidentiality, technical feasibility, arithmetic and units, bias and framing, and claims clearance.
